R360 — phase VMM real API lifetime audit
Date: 2026-10-13 (Asia/Tokyo)
Status: READ-ONLY SOURCE / SPEC REVIEW. Main GPU measurement 38293 was active. No build, test, AST/import, GPU, profiler, process/service, reset, Git, or source mutation was performed. This report is the only artifact created.

## Result

The source does not reproduce R337's concrete reservation-granularity UB: this revision queries the installed LLVM 7.1.1 device recommended granularity, device minimum, and context minimum, and builds its extent alignment from their checked LCM. Extent sizes and offsets, the reservation total, and the returned base are checked against the relevant minima before use. The installed SYCL extension requires those distinct constraints.

One failure-path concern remains, but the local API contract does not prove it is a current UB: a failed map is marked `maybe_attached`, then the extra-map rollback can issue `unmap` for that range. The SYCL extension requires unmap ranges to have been mapped. This is a conservative uncertain-ownership strategy, but calling unmap after a map exception is only justified if the provider may have partially established the map; the audited SYCL/UR wrapper forwards the Level Zero result and does not document partial-state semantics. Treat this as an unresolved failure-path/provider contract question, not as a confirmed production defect. No other concrete lifetime or ordering defect was found in this source-only pass.

## Evidence

Source W is `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/feat-phase-cache-stock-bench-20261013`, HEAD `410904c99d273435b5302fa8976cc667d17957f2` with the active uncommitted phase-cache source. The installed compiler/runtime tree is `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/MistVVK/XeStrata/.worktree/fix-xestrata-e32-host-handoff-20261011/.tools/intel-llvm-v711/install`; the primary local spec is Intel LLVM's `sycl/doc/extensions/experimental/sycl_ext_oneapi_virtual_mem.asciidoc`.

- `src/core/phase_cache_backend.cpp:20-31` checks VMM support for the selected device and every context device, then obtains device recommended, device minimum, and context minimum granularity. `PhaseCacheOwner::alignment` in `src/core/phase_cache_owner.cpp:20-29` computes a checked LCM with the 2-MiB extent policy and 256-byte payload stride. Reservation geometry is then checked against device and context minima at lines 90-108. The extension distinguishes physical allocation device granularity from context virtual-reservation granularity; `reserve_virtual_mem` requires address and byte count to be multiples of context minimum and declares violations undefined. Physical map address/length/offset use device minimum. Thus the previous R337 conditional issue is guarded in this source.
- `map_extent` at `src/core/phase_cache_owner.cpp:145-163` sets `maybe_attached=true` before invoking attach, so a failed/throwing attach retains its physical handle and cannot be mistaken for a known-unmapped clean extent. In `map_extras` lines 176-190, failed mapping drains and rolls back from the failed index through prior extents. `detach_extent` lines 164-175 invokes detach whenever `maybe_attached` is true. The SYCL extension says unmap requires a range previously mapped by `physical_mem::map`; unmapping an unmapped range is outside that precondition. This path therefore depends on undocumented/unchecked provider failure atomicity. Installed SYCL `sycl/source/detail/physical_mem_impl.hpp` forwards `urVirtualMemMap`; the Level Zero adapter in `unified-runtime/source/adapters/level_zero/virtual_mem.cpp:83-94` forwards to `zeVirtualMemMap`. Those wrappers do not add state tracking or explain partial mapping on an error. The backend contract in `phase_cache_owner.hpp` deliberately treats attach failure as uncertain, so a failure-injection test could validate retained ownership logic but cannot by itself establish real provider semantics.
- On normal paths, exact extent mappings use physical offset zero. Unmap precedes checked queue drain and physical-handle destruction (`phase_cache_owner.cpp:164-175); close detaches all extents before freeing the whole reserved range (`275-289`). This agrees with the extension note that destroying `physical_mem` does not unmap and its rule that `free_virtual_mem` must only free an unmapped range.
- Host owner release and current source-level producer/reader retirement are explicit, including the caller quiescence contract that backend drain alone is insufficient. Existing implementation and R337 reports describe the GEN/QUIT retirement ordering. This review did not repeat their broader caller-path audit or establish runtime queue/graph quiescence.

## Qualification boundary

The phase-owner CPU and server results reported by Main are not evidence of SYCL compilation or actual VMM behavior. This review did not inspect the restricted contract record, rerun primary CPU checks, or make any transfer/GPU claim. Real-provider granularity values, map-failure atomicity, actual successful map/unmap/free behavior, sourceLLVM build, and GPU qualification remain unverified. Main's active measurement must close before any such work.
